title: Where Do Attribution Graphs Fail? Identifying Prompt Classes Where Circuit Tracing Breaks Down

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: knowing which prompt types cause attribution graph failures guides researchers toward appropriate application, but the chain to direct safety improvement is indirect since it characterizes a tool limitation rather than a safety mechanism.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Using open-sourced circuit-tracing tools with a structured test battery of 80 prompts across 8 categories is intermediate. The tools are available but computing faithfulness scores requires understanding the attribution methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: construct 80 prompts across 8 pre-specified categories, compute faithfulness scores per category, identify structural predictors of low faithfulness. Systematic evaluation with clear measurable outputs.

novelty.reasoning: Anthropic released circuit tracing tools (2025) and published 'On the Biology of a Large Language Model' and 'Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models', defining mechanistic faithfulness metrics. While these papers discuss limitations, no systematic evaluation across structured prompt categories has been published. The open-sourced tools were released mid-2025, and the proposed systematic test battery (80 prompts, 8 categories, faithfulness score comparison) would be among the first independent evaluations of attribution graph reliability across prompt types. Self-Tracing extensions exist (recursivelabsai) but focus on recursive self-interpretation, not failure mode characterization.
